cell wall components of the fungus Paracocidioides brasillensis are able to induce the production of inflammatory macrophages, that are able to increase the antibody production against unrelated antigens.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the immunomodulatory activity of cell wall components of the fungus Paracocccidioides brasilliensis is mediated by a direct activation of macrophages, which in turn release inflammatory cytokines and augment the antibody production against unrelated antigens.

the cell wall components of the fungus, especially the F1 fraction, are able to induce a local and non‐progressive granulomatous reaction, which is characterized by a high production of inflammatory cytokines and the presence of (CD11/CD18)+ peritoneal cells, which are involved in the immunomodulation of antibody production.

the immunomodulatory activity of P. brasliensis CW components is mainly due to a β‐glucans‐containing fraction, which is capable of inducing a local and non‐progressive granulomatous reaction, and that the resulting inflammatory macrophages are able to modulate antibody production in the periphery.

the fungal cell wall β‐glucans, in the absence of the other fungal cell wall components, are the active components of P. braziliensis cell wall that are able to cause an early immunological disturbance in the host.

the cell wall components of the fungus P. brasiliensiis are capable of inducing an immune response in the host, leading to the production of antibodies against the fungus itself, but also against unrelated antigens.
